verdict.rationale: Orb's docs show hybrid subscription-plus-usage pricing configurable from the UI: flat-rate, usage-based and seat pricing, credit allotments with automatic top-ups, and minimums and maximums that approximate commitments and caps. The specific tiered, volume, graduated and per-unit price models are never named in the evidence, so only part of the story is documented. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of tiered, volume, graduated and per-unit price models; explicit commitment and overage mechanics; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, I can price with tiered, volume, graduated, per-unit, and hybrid subscription-plus-usage models — including credits, commitments, and overage — without custom code

citations.quote: whether you're using flat-rate subscriptions, usage-based pricing, pricing on seats, or you've implemented custom billing logic
Minimums: Ensures a minimum charge is applied. Maximums: Caps the charge at a certain amount.
Customers can either buy tokens on-demand, or set up an automatic top-up to buy tokens on their behalf when they're depleted.
You can create a subscription either from the Orb UI or via the subscription creation API endpoint.
Subscription Edits let you change a single subscription's pricing configuration directly from Orb's web interface or via the API
